低音大號擁有渾厚、深沉且富有威權感的音色，音質溫潤而帶有適度的金屬光澤。其音域主: The sousaphone has a full, deep and authoritative timbre, warm in quality with a moderate metallic sheen. Its range lies mostly in the bass to low-middle register, and it produces a steady, powerful low sound that lays a firm musical foundation for the band. The instrument resonates through its huge bell, throwing the sound waves outward in all directions with excellent carrying power. Where the traditional tuba is sharper in timbre, the sousaphone is broader and softer; against the cello its tone is heavier and strongly brassy. In a band its sound is distinct and powerful, clearly heard by listeners far away, both solemn and approachable.

蘇沙號屬銅管樂器，傳統琴身以黃銅板製成，常見黃色或銀色，並可鍍銀、上漆或鍍金。自: The sousaphone is a brass instrument; its body was traditionally made of sheet brass, usually yellow or silver in colour, and may be silver-plated, lacquered or gold-plated. From the middle of the 20th century lighter materials such as fibreglass and plastic have also been used, being lighter, more durable and cheaper. It sounds from the player's lip vibration, entering the tube through a large cup mouthpiece; the source gives no materials for the mouthpiece, valves, detachable bell or gooseneck.
蘇沙號約1893年由J. W. Pepper依約翰·菲利普·蘇沙指示，從海利孔改: The sousaphone was made around 1893 by J. W. Pepper to the instructions of John Philip Sousa, adapted from the helicon. Sousa wanted the bass to pass over the band's heads to the audience; the early instruments had an upright bell and were mainly for concert use. In 1898 C. G. Conn also built the instrument, which then became Sousa's usual choice. The U.S. Navy Band adopted it in 1908, and that year Conn brought out a version bent 90 degrees with the bell facing forward, which became the later standard. Fibreglass and plastic instruments appeared from the mid-20th century, and after 1961 several makers offered fibreglass models; bell sizes ran from 22 inches to a standard of 26 inches by the mid-1930s. European tours and the Philippine Constabulary Band carried it abroad.
蘇沙號（sousaphone）是氣鳴銅管樂器，屬低音號家族，H-S編號423.2: The sousaphone is an aerophone of the brass family, H-S number 423.232. Its tube is bent into a circle that wraps around the player's body, the coil rests on the shoulder, the valves sit in front and the bell faces forward and up; the sound comes from lip vibration through a cup mouthpiece. In 1893 J. W. Pepper made it to the instructions of the American composer and bandmaster John Philip Sousa, adapting the helicon, and it takes his name. Because it is easy to carry and projects its sound forward, it is common in marching bands and other kinds of music.
